title: CT-bMPS: Approximate Tensor Network Contraction with Boundary MPS on Contraction Trees
abstract: We introduce contraction tree boundary matrix product states (CT-bMPS), a scalable approximate contraction method for general closed tensor networks. CT-bMPS represents the boundary tensor and its complementary environment at each edge of a contraction tree as matrix product states. This representation allows local compression based on a reduced transition matrix to incorporate environment information along arbitrary contraction trees, while keeping the time and memory costs polynomial in the network size and bond dimension. We benchmark the method on a variety of models and applications, including Ising partition functions, random tensor networks, kicked Ising dynamics, and quantum error correction decoding. These benchmarks demonstrate improved accuracy and computational efficiency over existing general-purpose approximate contraction methods, together with the ability to handle larger and more complex networks. Optimized contraction trees and environment updates substantially improve accuracy without increasing the bond dimension. These results establish CT-bMPS as a general and scalable approximation framework with flexible contraction orders and environment-based compression for a wide range of applications.
summary: This paper introduces CT-bMPS, a scalable approximation technique for contracting complex, general closed tensor networks. By representing boundaries as MPS and incorporating an 'environment' message, it significantly improves accuracy while maintaining polynomial computational scaling. This framework is highly valuable for simulating diverse quantum systems, from statistical mechanics models to quantum error correction codes.
main_problem: The paper addresses the computational challenge of exactly contracting general closed tensor networks (TNs), which is generally \#P-hard.
main_result: The proposed CT-bMPS framework provides a general and scalable approximation method that improves accuracy and efficiency over existing techniques for complex TN contractions.
method: It uses a contraction tree structure and represents boundary tensors as Matrix Product States (MPS), incorporating an 'environment' (opposite MPS message) to guide local compression and improve accuracy.
model_or_system: The method is general, applicable to any system formulated as a closed TN, including Ising partition functions, random TNs, kicked Ising dynamics, and quantum error correction decoding.
key_observables: Relative error, logical error rates (in QEC), contraction time, and computational FLOPs.
important_parameters: Bond dimension ($\chi$), network size ($L$), and the choice of contraction tree/index order.
main_assumptions: The accuracy depends on the choice of the contraction tree and the global index order; the environment update procedure introduces memory overhead.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the mechanism of CT-bMPS contraction using contraction trees and boundary MPS messages, comparing its performance against ordinary contraction methods for the Ising model.
paper_structure: The paper introduces CT-bMPS, details its use of contraction trees and environment-based MPS representations, benchmarks it on various physical models (Ising, QEC), and compares its performance metrics (accuracy vs. cost) against state-of-the-art methods.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, general-purpose numerical tool for simulating quantum many-body systems whose Hamiltonians or partition functions can be mapped onto complex tensor network structures, which is crucial for simulating dynamics beyond simple 1D chains.

figures.caption: Figure 1: CT-bMPS overview. The input TN is shown on the lower plane; the contraction tree above it groups subsets of its tensors. Each tree edge carries a boundary MPS rather than a dense tensor. Messages in both directions represent the two complementary parts of the TN. The opposite message serves as an environment for local truncation, and pairing the two messages gives the scalar.

Figure 2: Ordinary CT-bMPS. (a) Two incoming boundary MPS messages A and B form an outgoing message C at a contraction tree node. (b) Four local index patterns around the core tensor T. Indices L and R occur in only one input and survive in C. An internal index I is summed and has no output site. A shared hyperedge H with an outside owner survives as one site of C. Dashed colored input sites indicate transfer into the solid output site.

Figure 3: Environment CT-bMPS. (a) The opposite boundary MPS provides the environment E for combining the incoming messages A and B. (b) Local truncation at the cut between j and k. Contracting the tensors to the left of the cut gives K, while Q is formed from the core tensor T.

Figure 4: The 6 × 6 × 6 Ising model at β = 0.3. Relative scalar error is plotted against (a) contraction time and (b) peak process RSS. FLOPs denotes the CT-bMPS path obtained by simulated annealing to minimize exact contraction FLOPs; xyz denotes a geometric sweep of the lattice. Markers indicate χ. CT-bMPS uses native spin hyperedges; HAC and CATN use pairwise representations.
